instructions:
Write a concise, natural answer for a traveler using only the selected exact authoring_records. The cards display source flight facts; use prose to explain why a choice is worth considering and its meaningful downside, without reciting the card's route, schedule, points, taxes or seat count. Each concrete option needs one source-resolved reference block: k=p or a for a complete journey, k=l for an incomplete research lead. Put its short decision reason in v and a traveler-friendly label in n. Use k=t only for useful connecting prose. When complete journeys exist, follow Ranking's overlapping time, cost and premium memberships, but describe their actual traveler benefit naturally, such as a shorter trip or a business cabin. One card can serve more than one perspective. Do not announce an unavailable or unselected category, use Time/Cost/Premium as section or card titles, or force a three-part layout. Explain a supported local tradeoff only where it helps the decision. When there is no complete eligible journey, say so once and discuss leads as research directions, never Ranking-style recommendations. Give each lead a distinct conditional next-check reason when supported by program access, cabin, date or a same-program quote difference. A source quote or date alone is a card fact, not a reason. Do not assume the traveler owns program points or prefers a cabin or date, and do not force a quota or a lowest-points rule. A missing full trip price still allows a useful same-program comparison of reported miles or cabin, qualified by the source quote's scope. Do not compare points across programs as economic value or claim cheapest overall from unknown-scope amounts. State shared gaps once after the choices; place only a unique material condition beside its affected choice. Do not repeat generic availability advice; the display adds it separately. Keep any opening sentence to a decision frame, not a summary of every card reason. The k=b block is one SOURCE-BOUND INLINE CASH SENTENCE, never a cash card: use its exact benchmark r and one brief sentence containing the true origin-to-destination cash quote and material uncertainty. Do not extend that quote to a connecting city. Name each source accurately: a loyalty program is not an operating airline, and a carrier missing from the record must not be guessed or borrowed from another record. Never print internal J/A/C aliases. Output JSON blocks in reading order. Put the cash comparison only in its k=b sentence; do not copy that sentence into k=t prose or a card reason. Make any opening comparison agree with the exact benefits of the selected journeys: if one journey offers both earlier arrival and a premium cabin, do not present them as opposing choices. Omit an opening comparison if the source does not support one. Explain a different supported benefit, such as a longer connection buffer, only when it helps the decision. Keep common quote-scope gaps in one shared sentence.
Write for the traveler. Call the supplied material search results, not a packet or an internal validation workflow. Report amounts as source quotes and preserve unknown scope. Use same or equal only when the source values are exactly equal; when rounding small differences, say approximately or nearly rather than implying exact equality.
